prompt: On nodes using the same OS/architecture, you want to identify one exact platform image manifest rather than a mutable tag. Which registry reference should you use?

options.explanation: latest is a tag, not an automatic update mechanism. It can be moved when authorized publication changes it.
A version tag is still a name. Registry immutability policies may restrict updates, but the tag text itself does not encode content.
Correct. A digest is the hash of the manifest's bytes; it can only ever refer to that exact content.

options.text: The image ID shown by `docker images`
options.explanation: That local ID is the config digest on your machine; registries and deployments reference manifests by their digest.

workedExample: A platform manifest digest identifies the manifest bytes; its descriptors identify config and layers. A multi-platform index digest instead fixes a set whose selected platform can differ by node. Referencing by digest does not guarantee future availability, publisher authenticity or identical runtime environment.

prompt: Which statements about content-addressed image layers are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: Identical layer blobs can be reused rather than downloaded/stored again where the content store supports it
options.explanation: Correct. Matching content digests enable reuse; actual physical sharing depends on registry, content-store and snapshotter implementation.

options.text: A client can detect a corrupted or tampered layer after download
options.explanation: Correct. It recomputes the SHA-256 and compares it with the digest in the manifest.

options.text: Pushing a new tag for an existing image changes its layer digests
options.explanation: Tagging only creates a new name for the same manifest; no bytes change, so no digest changes.

options.text: Updating only your application code usually means pulling only the top layer(s)
options.explanation: Correct. Lower layers already present locally are skipped because their digests match.

workedExample: Matching digest-addressed blobs can be reused and verified against expected content. Adding a tag does not alter blob bytes. An app-only update can reuse unchanged cached base layers, though manifests/config and changed blobs still need resolving. Digest integrity is distinct from trusting who published the image.
